app.title: ALIGNED – Reform Track
app.summary: A person narrows a fixed table of coded sentences to a range of years. They then choose how to split the sentences into groups: a one-click preset, checkboxes for dimension and effort type, a free pick of topics, or a theoretical lens that groups topics into primary and secondary interests. They switch between yearly average scores drawn as lines and period averages ranked as bars, with headline numbers above. Finally they download the chart and the numbers behind it, and copy a citation for the dataset.

task.text: Compare the average evaluative score of coded document sentences across thematic groups and over the years, and export the chart and its numbers.

data.text: A spreadsheet of evaluative sentences from yearly reports. Each sentence carries a year, a two-level topic classification, an effort type and a coded score on a signed scale.
data.item: one evaluative sentence from a yearly report, coded with a score from -1 to +1 and classified by dimension, topic and effort type

stage.text: analysing and comparing hand-coded sentence scores after coding, before writing up

mechanism.text: Sidebar controls are split into three families that exclude each other (the one touched last clears the others). One resolver turns them into groups of sentences, and those groups drive both the stat cards and the main chart. A view toggle switches the chart between yearly mean lines and ranked mean bars, and the current view can be downloaded as an image and a CSV.

field.text: core-sentence content analysis of policy reports in political sociology

workflow.name: compare average scores of coded items across groups and over time

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: A two-handled year slider limits every view to a range of report years.

Presets (Full Picture, Pol. vs Econ., Dom. vs Intl., World-Systems), Political/Economic and Domestic/International checkboxes, a searchable topic multiselect, or primary/secondary interest groupings that can be broken down into single topics. Whichever family is touched last takes over and clears the others.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Stat cards show the mean score, the number of sentences, the year span and the share of negative sentences for the current selection.
The chart shows yearly mean lines per group (with zero, min and max guides) or period means as ranked horizontal bars. With nothing selected it shows the overall line or a ranking by topic.
Buttons download the chart as SVG (or HTML if that fails) and the series or ranking as CSV. An expander gives APA and BibTeX citations for the dataset version.

distinctive: The three control families exclude each other, so the sidebar never shows a control that has no effect on the chart.
Checking dimensions and effort types together follows fixed rules: both efforts with both dimensions cancel out, while one dimension with both efforts splits into two lines.
An optional theoretical lens groups topics into primary and secondary interests, each of which can be broken down into its single topics.
Scores are on a signed scale from -1 to +1 with neutral sentences left out, so the charts are fixed around a zero reference line.
Each export comes with a citation tied to the dataset version, for reuse as a citable data set.

parts.title: Grouping controls
parts.summary: Checkboxes, a searchable topic picker and the interest lens. The family used last decides which groups of sentences are compared.

parts.title: Headline stat cards
parts.summary: Shows the mean score, the sentence count, the year span and the share of negative sentences for the current selection.
